description: How to reuse forks in each catalog category as building blocks. Each catalog repo entry carries `reuse` (method, pinned install lines, licence note); these notes add category-level guidance. Always pin `commit`, keep SPDX headers, and prefer the upstream package registry when the fork is an unmodified mirror.

methods.forge: Solidity: `forge install Blockchains/<fork>@<commit>` + a remapping; share one OpenZeppelin (Blockchains/openzeppelin-contracts@<tag>) across blocks.
methods.npm-git: Single JS/TS package: `npm i github:Blockchains/<fork>#<commit>` (needs a `prepare` build script if it ships TypeScript sources).
methods.npm-registry: JS/TS monorepo: install the published package; use the fork commit to read and compare source.
methods.go-replace: Go: keep the upstream module path and add `replace <module> => github.com/Blockchains/<fork> <commit>`.
methods.source: Applications, nodes and specs: build from source (`install_commands`) or run the upstream release; integrate over RPC/API.

categories.account-abstraction: ERC-4337 EntryPoint, smart accounts and paymasters. Use the EntryPoint version deployed on your chain (v0.7/v0.8 addresses differ); import interfaces via forge, not copies. See forge-example-gasless-membership for a working paymaster + viem client.
categories.ai-agents: Agent frameworks and toolkits. Run them as separate services or install the published package; give them chain data via blockchainlab-mcp instead of hand-written RPC tools. Check licences, several are copyleft.
categories.analytics: Analytics/explorer tooling. Usually apps: deploy them, or use their queries/schemas as references; for ready-made datasets prefer blockchainlab-api.
categories.bitcoin-lightning: Bitcoin and Lightning nodes, wallets and libraries. Talk to nodes over RPC (bitcoind JSON-RPC, LND gRPC/REST); import libraries (btcd, rust-bitcoin, bitcoinjs) at a pinned commit or from their registries. Never reuse test keys.
categories.bridges-interop: Bridge/messaging protocols. Integrate through the deployed contracts and official SDKs; copying bridge code is high-risk, so pin and audit.
categories.chains-protocols: L1 protocol implementations. Run the node or use its client SDK; import only well-scoped libraries (crypto, encoding) from them.
categories.clients-nodes: Execution/consensus clients and node software. Build from source (`install_commands`) or use upstream release binaries/containers; integrate via JSON-RPC/Engine API. Go clients can be used as libraries via a `replace` directive (e.g. go-ethereum's ethclient, abi, crypto).
categories.cosmos: Cosmos SDK, CometBFT and IBC. Go modules: use a `replace` directive to the pinned fork commit or the tagged upstream version; scaffold chains with ignite/cli.
categories.cryptography-mpc: MPC/threshold signing libraries. Use as libraries at a pinned commit; never roll your own parameters; review security advisories before production.
categories.data-registries: Registries (chain lists, token lists, standards). Consume the JSON files at the pinned commit (raw URLs in `raw_base`) or via blockchainlab-api datasets that already normalise them.
categories.defi: DeFi protocol contracts and SDKs. Integrate with deployed protocols through their interfaces (forge install for interfaces, npm SDKs for routing). Many are BUSL/GPL: check `license_note` before copying any core contract.
categories.dev-tooling: Frameworks, testing and devops tools (Foundry, Hardhat, Brownie…). Install the released tool; the fork is for reading source and pinning behaviour.
categories.enterprise-ledgers: Permissioned ledgers (Fabric, Besu…). Run the network from samples; reuse chaincode/contract samples as templates.
categories.ethereum-evm: EVM libraries and specs (ethers, viem, web3.py, specs, EIPs). Prefer the published package; use the specs repos as test-vector sources.
categories.hedera: Hedera SDKs and services. Use the published SDKs (`@hashgraph/sdk` etc.); see blockchainlab-starters/starters/hedera-token-sdk.
categories.identity: DID/identity standards and libraries. Use published packages; conform to the W3C/EIP spec the repo implements.
categories.indexing: Indexers/subgraphs. Run as a service; copy subgraph manifests/schemas as templates.
categories.l2-rollups: Rollup stacks and contracts. Deploy via the stack's tooling; import interfaces (forge) to integrate with deployed L2 bridges; node software as in clients-nodes.
categories.languages-compilers: Compilers and languages (solc, Vyper, Noir, Cairo, Move). Install releases; pin compiler versions in your project config.
categories.move: Move language/frameworks (Aptos/Sui). Add as a Move.toml git dependency with `rev = <commit>`.
categories.nft: NFT standards and marketplaces. Import standards from OpenZeppelin; for a complete USD-priced membership NFT use Blockchains/forge-usd-priced-membership-nft.
categories.oracles: Oracle contracts/nodes (Chainlink…). Import feed interfaces (AggregatorV3Interface) via forge; use deployed feed addresses; run nodes from releases.
categories.p2p-storage: IPFS/libp2p/Filecoin/Swarm. Run nodes from releases; use libp2p/kubo as Go libraries via `replace`, or JS clients from npm.
categories.payments: Payment protocols/apps. Integrate via API/SDK; reuse UI flows as references.
categories.polkadot: Substrate/Polkadot SDK. Rust crates via `cargo add … --git … --rev <commit>`; keep all Substrate crates on the same commit.
categories.security: Analysers and audit tooling (Slither, Mythril…). Install the released tool and run it in CI; reuse detectors/rules as references.
categories.smart-contract-libraries: Contract libraries (OpenZeppelin, solmate, account-abstraction). `forge install Blockchains/<fork>@<tag>` with one shared remapping; never mix two OpenZeppelin major versions.
categories.solana: Solana programs and SDKs. Rust crates via cargo git rev (keep solana-* crates aligned); JS via npm; Anchor projects via their CLI.
categories.wallets: Wallet apps and libraries. Reuse wallet libraries (key management, connectors) from registries; wallet apps are references for UX, not dependencies.
categories.zk: ZK circuits, provers and DSLs. Pin exact prover/circuit versions (verifying keys change between versions); see blockchainlab-starters circom-zk-proof and noir-zk-proof.
